items.text: Language version and copy provided
items.detail: Language used; confirmation that the employee received a copy.

items.text: If the employee declines to sign, don't withhold pay or exit documents. Record the refusal, give them the obligations reminder anyway, and tell Legal if the departure is flagged.

notes: Use the certification for every departure, not just suspected ones. Consistent use is part of the 'reasonable secrecy measures' that trade-secret protection depends on (DTSA, GeschGehG, Taiwan Trade Secrets Act, China AUCL).

Never ask the employee to state that they have not filed a complaint with, or given information to, a government agency, and never require them to notify the Company before contacting one. The SEC treats such wording in exit documents as impeding whistleblowers (Rule 21F-17).
The DTSA immunity notice must appear here or in a referenced policy; without it, the Company can't recover exemplary damages or attorney fees from the employee in a DTSA case.
Signing is never a condition of final pay, a relieving letter, a termination certificate or an ROE. A refusal is recorded and escalated, never bargained over.
Personal devices: disclosure first, supervised removal second. Self-deletion before disclosure can destroy evidence and breach a legal hold.

For flagged departures, pair the form with a DLP lookback, forensic imaging before re-imaging and a Legal-approved reminder letter. False statements on the form become key evidence if misappropriation is found later.
Use the local-language version as the signed original in China, Taiwan, Vietnam, Germany and Israel, and keep the signed form in the personnel file for the retention period (DS-03).

countryNotes.us: Include the DTSA notice and the Rule 21F-17 and NLRA Section 7 carve-outs, and cite the relevant state trade-secret act in the reminder letter. Remind foreign nationals leaving the US that export-control obligations stay with them.
countryNotes.us-ca: No non-compete or non-solicit references (B&P 16600, 16600.5; LC 925); include the Gov Code 12964.5 carve-out and respect the LC 2870 invention carve-out. Give a CCPA notice at collection covering device review, and get all-party consent before recording the exit meeting.
countryNotes.us-co: Refer only to non-competes that meet C.R.S. 8-2-113 ($130,014 in 2026 when enforced, trade-secret purpose, separate notice); presenting a void covenant is a misdemeanor with a $5,000-per-worker penalty. Deduct unreturned property only under a prior written agreement.
countryNotes.us-nc: Written, signed non-competes and non-solicits supported by consideration can be restated, and the NC Trade Secrets Protection Act (G.S. 66-152) supports fast injunctions. No deductions for unreturned equipment without a G.S. 95-25.8 authorization.
countryNotes.us-tx: Reaffirm enforceable Texas covenants (Bus. & Com. Code 15.50) and TUTSA protection. Deduct unreturned property only with prior written authorization (Labor Code 61.018), and delete biometric templates under CUBI.
countryNotes.us-wa: Until 29 June 2027, refer only to noncompetes that meet RCW 49.62; from 30 June 2027 all are void, and threatening enforcement costs at least $5,000 plus fees. Include the Silenced No More carve-out (RCW 49.44.211) and rely on the WA UTSA and DTSA.
countryNotes.ca: Ontario bans non-competes below the C-suite (ESA s.67.2), and BC courts rarely enforce them, so certify confidentiality and narrow non-solicits only. Disclose exit review in the Ontario electronic monitoring policy and the BC PIPA notice.
countryNotes.de: Issue in German or bilingual. Forensic review needs a works agreement for the tools (§87(1) no.6 BetrVG), a DPIA and proportionality; GeschGehG protection depends on appropriate secrecy measures such as this form, and any post-contractual non-compete needs Karenzentschädigung and a separate letter.
countryNotes.il: Issue in Hebrew. Device review follows Isakov (a written policy, proportionality, transparency, no private mailboxes), and trade secrets are protected under the Commercial Torts Law; non-competes pass only the Checkpoint legitimate-interest test.
countryNotes.in: Device review can rely on DPDP s.7(i) (protecting trade secrets, preventing corporate espionage) with notice and proportionality. Post-exit non-competes are void (Contract Act s.27), and the relieving letter is never conditional on signing.
countryNotes.tw: Issue in Traditional Chinese, with the Trade Secrets Act and National Security Act core key technology reminder and any Cross-Strait Act travel-approval duty. Enforce a non-compete only if it meets Art. 9-1, and give a PDPA notice for any review.
countryNotes.cn: Issue in Chinese, with the AUCL confidentiality reminder and the signed handover checklist. Activate or release any non-compete in writing, give a PIPL notice for device review, and get separate consent before review results are transferred abroad.
countryNotes.vn: Issue in Vietnamese, relying on the LC Art. 21(2) confidentiality agreement and IP Law trade-secret protection; post-exit non-competes are of uncertain enforceability. Exit review must be disclosed monitoring under PDPL Art. 25, and asset recovery can't delay the 14-working-day settlement.

templates.name: Reduction-in-force communications pack
templates.purpose: Everything managers, HR and Communications need to announce a reduction in force consistently: preparation, the notification-meeting script, what not to say, the employee FAQ, the survivor meeting, external holding lines and the internal announcement, all sequenced against WARN and country consultation deadlines. It keeps every message aligned with the approved business rationale, the selection record and the Company's public disclosures.
templates.audience: Managers delivering notifications; HRBPs and Employee Relations; Internal and Corporate Communications; Investor Relations; Legal and the Disclosure Committee; sales and account leaders who handle customer outreach.
templates.when: Prepared once the RIF is approved and selection is final (OF-03, T-RIF-SELECTION), and used from manager briefing (D-3) through survivor follow-ups (D+14). In countries that require consultation or authority notice, no individual is told they are selected until that country's legal gate opens.
templates.owner: HR (RIF program lead) with Corporate Communications; Legal and the Disclosure Committee approve every external and internal message before use

sections.title: Manager preparation checklist
sections.intro: Complete before notification day. The HRBP confirms each item in the RIF tracker.

items.text: Attend the manager briefing and rehearse the notification script with your HRBP at least once.
Confirm your notification list, meeting times, rooms or video links, and the HRBP attending each meeting. Each meeting is one-to-one and lasts 10-15 minutes.
Check each packet: local-language letter, severance offer and release, benefits summary, equity statement, FAQ and contact sheet, with names, dates and amounts verified.
Confirm with IT when access will be cut (meeting start or end) and that courier return kits are ready for remote employees.
Make sure Immigration is available on notification day for visa holders, and that the list of affected visa holders has gone to Immigration.

Keep everything confidential: no hints, no early warnings and no changes to lists. Report any leak to your HRBP immediately. RIF information may be material non-public information, and everyone involved is on the insider list.
Know your country's gate: in Germany, China (Art. 41), Taiwan (mass redundancy), Vietnam and India (retrenchment of workers), notifications wait until consultation and authority filings allow them.
Plan your own support: EAP contact, a buffer between meetings, and time with your HRBP at the end of the day.
Thanks for joining. I have some difficult news to share, and I'm going to get straight to it.

As [Company] announced [today / this morning], we are reducing [the size of / specific teams in] [organization] because of [approved business reason]. I'm sorry to tell you that your position is one of those affected.
items.detail: Use only the approved business reason, word for word.

items.text: This decision is based on [the business needs of the team / the elimination of the [X] function], not on your performance.
items.detail: Say this only if it is true for everyone in the group and matches the selection records.

items.text: Your employment will end on [date]. [Until then you will be on paid [notice / garden leave] and are not expected to work.] [Until then we'll ask you to help transition [x].]

[HRBP name] will take you through your package, which includes [severance / notice pay], benefits and equity, and you'll have everything in writing. You have [45 days / the local review period] to consider the separation agreement, and we encourage you to talk to a lawyer or adviser before you sign.
Your access to [systems] [ends at the end of this meeting / will end on [date]]. [HRBP name] will explain how to collect your personal items and return equipment.
I know this is a lot to take in. What questions can I answer now? Anything we can't answer today, [HRBP name] will follow up in writing by [date].
Thank you for everything you've contributed here. I'm sorry this is the news.
Don't say 'This wasn't my decision', 'I fought for you' or 'You're lucky, the package is good'. It undercuts the decision and suggests other motives.
Don't give reasons that differ from the documented selection criteria, and don't compare the employee with colleagues who are staying.
Don't mention age, 'fresh blood', energy, individual salary cost, family, leave, pregnancy, disability, visa status, complaints, union activity or any other protected characteristic or activity.
Don't promise anything that hasn't been approved: rehire, references beyond policy, more severance, contractor work or immigration outcomes.

Don't discuss financial results, other teams, further rounds or anything not yet public; that is MNPI and a Regulation FD risk. If asked about future cuts, say: 'I can't speculate. [HRBP] can tell you what has been announced.'

Don't suggest the employee resign or call the exit 'voluntary'. In China and Vietnam especially, pressured resignations are a known way of avoiding severance, and authorities and courts treat them as unlawful terminations.
Don't notify anyone by email, chat, text, voicemail or group call, or let people learn of it from an access cut or the press.

sections.title: Employee FAQ
sections.intro: Share this FAQ with affected employees in their packet and at their personal email, in the local language. Update it daily during the first week.

items.text: Why was my role selected?
items.detail: Answer: the decision followed [the elimination of the function / defined business criteria] applied consistently across [the decisional unit]. US employees aged 40+ receive the OWBPA disclosure of the job titles and ages of those selected and not selected in the decisional unit.

items.text: When is my last day, and will I be paid through my notice period?
items.detail: Answer: [date]. You will be paid [through the WARN / Cal-WARN / WA mini-WARN notice period / through ESA and contractual notice in Canada / through the statutory notice period in your country], whether or not you are asked to work.

items.text: When will I receive my final pay?
items.detail: Answer by jurisdiction: CA and CO on the separation date, including accrued vacation; TX within 6 calendar days; NC next regular payday; WA end of the pay period; ON later of 7 days or next payday; BC within 48 hours; India within 2 working days; Taiwan immediately, with severance within 30 days; China at termination; Vietnam within 30 days for restructuring; Germany and Israel on the normal pay date.

items.text: What severance will I receive, and what do I need to do to get it?
items.detail: Answer: statutory amounts (notice, statutory severance, payable leave) are paid regardless. The additional severance of [formula] is paid in exchange for signing the separation agreement within [review period]; in the US, you have 7 days to revoke after signing.

items.text: What happens to my health insurance and other benefits?
items.detail: Answer: coverage ends on [date]. [The Company will pay [X] months of COBRA premiums.] Ontario benefits continue through the ESA notice period; local plans follow the country summary in your packet.

items.text: What happens to my equity?
items.detail: Answer: vesting stops on your termination date unless your package says otherwise, and you have [3 months] to exercise vested options. ESPP contributions for the current period are refunded. The Insider Trading Policy still applies to any MNPI you have.

items.text: I'm on a work visa. What happens to my status?
items.detail: Answer: Immigration will contact you within 1 business day. H-1B holders generally have a grace period of up to 60 days (or until their I-94 expires, if sooner), and the Company will offer to pay reasonable return transportation. Green card processes in progress will stop; outside the US, work permits and residence cards are cancelled under local rules (verify each case).

items.text: Will I get a reference? What will the Company tell future employers?
items.detail: Answer: we confirm dates of employment and job title (and salary with your consent) under our References policy. Local documents: India relieving and experience letters, Taiwan service certificate, China termination certificate, Germany Arbeitszeugnis on request.

items.text: Can I apply for other roles here, or be rehired later?
items.detail: Answer: yes, you can apply for open roles [now / after your last day] and will be marked eligible for rehire. China Art. 41 layoffs carry a 6-month rehiring priority, and retrenched Indian 'workers' have a 1-year re-employment preference.

items.text: Can I claim unemployment benefits?
items.detail: Answer: usually yes. We will provide the documents you need: California DE 2320 and UI Code 1089 notice, Canada ROE, Germany Arbeitsbescheinigung, Taiwan involuntary separation certificate, Vietnam social insurance book.

items.text: What support is available to me?
items.detail: Answer: [outplacement for X months], the EAP, and job-search time during notice: Ontario 3 unpaid job-seeking days; Taiwan job-seeking leave of up to 2 paid days a week during notice (LSA Art. 16).

items.text: Who can I contact with questions after today?
items.detail: Answer: the RIF help desk at [email], your HRBP [name], the benefits administrator [contact] and Stock Admin [contact]. We'll send updated FAQs to your personal email.

items.text: Earlier today, we told [number / some] colleagues in [team] that their roles are affected by the reduction [Company] announced.
items.detail: Name individuals only with their agreement.

items.text: These were hard decisions, made because [approved business reason]. They are not a reflection on the people who are leaving.
Our colleagues who are leaving are being treated with respect and are receiving [notice, severance, benefits support and outplacement].
Here's what changes for us: [reassigned responsibilities, new priorities, what we stop doing]. I'll meet each of you one-to-one this week to go through your work.
I can't discuss individual colleagues' situations. Please be respectful and don't share internal details or speculation outside the Company.
[Only if the Disclosure Committee confirms it is true:] We have no plans for further reductions beyond what was announced today.
items.detail: Otherwise say: 'I can't speculate about the future, but I'll tell you what I can, when I can.'

items.text: If you have concerns, talk to me, [HRBP name] or use Speak Up. The EAP is available at [contact].
Hold survivor meetings within 2 hours of the last notification in each team, by video or in person. Avoid 'fresh start' or 'stronger team' language.

sections.title: External holding statement and internal announcement
sections.intro: Legal, Corporate Communications, IR and the Disclosure Committee approve all text before use.

items.text: Customer and partner holding statement (reactive; account teams use it only when asked): '[Company] has made organizational changes to focus on [priority areas]. We remain fully committed to our customers and partners, and your support and delivery commitments are unchanged. [Your point of contact going forward is [name].] We don't comment on individual employment matters.'

Media and analyst holding line (authorized spokespeople only): '[Company] is reducing about [number] positions, about [x]% of its workforce, as part of [reason]. We are supporting affected employees with [severance, benefits continuation and transition support]. [Further information is in our Form 8-K / press release dated [date].]' All other employees refer inquiries to [Corporate Communications email].

Internal announcement (from [CEO / function leader]), subject 'Changes to our organization': 'Team, today we are making difficult changes to [organization] because [approved business reason]. We are reducing about [number] roles across [functions / locations]. Everyone directly affected in [countries notifying today] will hear from their manager by [time and time zone] today. In [countries in consultation], we are beginning [consultation with employee representatives / the required notification process] and will share more when it is complete.'

'Colleagues who are leaving will receive [severance, extended benefits, outplacement and equity treatment], and every affected employee will be treated with respect. If you are not affected, your manager will meet with your team today. Please treat departing colleagues with care, and don't share internal details externally until [Company] has announced them publicly. The Insider Trading Policy applies to this information until then. Thank you, [Name].'

Publish the internal announcement only after any required 8-K or press release is public, or at the same moment, and only after the first notifications in the earliest time zone have started. Don't post it to channels that include contractors or external guests.

sections.title: Timing and sequencing checklist
sections.intro: Work backwards from the latest legal gate. D0 is the first notification day in each country.

items.text: Disclosure Committee check before any public statement, internal announcement, WARN notice or authority filing: decide whether the RIF or its charges are material and require an 8-K (Item 2.05 within 4 business days of committing to the plan, or 7.01/8.01) or a press release, and set timing against earnings and trading windows.
items.detail: Add everyone who knows about the RIF to the insider list and blackout until it is public.

items.text: Legal confirms, for each country, the consultation and notification steps and the earliest date an individual may be notified. That date is the gate in the RIF tracker.

US WARN: count employment losses per site over 30 and 90 days; give 60 days' notice to affected employees, the state dislocated-worker unit and the chief local elected official, or pay in lieu. Cal-WARN: 75+ employee establishments, 50+ layoffs within 30 days, notices with SB 617 content. WA mini-WARN: 50+ WA employees, notice to ESD. CO, NC and TX: federal WARN only.
US group releases: prepare the OWBPA decisional-unit disclosure exhibit (45 days to consider, 7 to revoke) and run the adverse-impact review before finalizing the lists (T-RIF-SELECTION).

Germany: inform and consult the works council in writing, attempt an Interessenausgleich and agree a Sozialplan where the operational-change thresholds are met, and complete the §102 BetrVG hearing. File a complete mass dismissal notice with the Agentur für Arbeit after consultation ends and before any notice is received; defects make every dismissal void. Notices must be wet-ink.

China: for Art. 41 layoffs (20+ employees or 10%+), explain the plan to the union or all employees 30 days in advance, consider their views and report the plan to the labor bureau (Shanghai: notify worker representatives 30 days before filing from Aug 2026). Notify the union before any unilateral termination (Art. 43). Most MNCs run mutual termination programs instead.

India: for 'workers' with 1+ year's service, give 1 month's written notice with reasons or pay in lieu, notify the appropriate government (IR Code s.70), pay 15 days' wages per year plus 15 days' wages into the Worker Re-skilling Fund, and apply last-in-first-out by category unless reasons are recorded. Managers exit under their contracts.

Taiwan: file the Employment Services Act Art. 33 notice 10 days before each Art. 11 separation. Where Mass Redundancy Protection Act thresholds are met, give the plan to the authority, the union or representatives and employees 60 days ahead and negotiate within 10 days. Give Art. 16 notice and job-seeking leave.

Canada: an Ontario mass termination (50+ in 4 weeks) needs Form 1 filed with the Director and posted, with 8, 12 or 16 weeks' notice. A BC group termination (50+ in 2 months) needs notice to employees, any union and the Minister, with 8, 12 or 16 weeks. Individual ESA and common-law notice applies on top.

Vietnam: prepare the Art. 44 labour-use plan, consult the grassroots union and publish the plan within 15 days. Give 30 days' prior notice to the provincial People's Committee and the employees, calculate the job-loss allowance and settle within 30 days.

Israel: no WARN-type regime, but hold an individual hearing (with a written invitation) for each affected employee before the decision, get permits for protected employees, and consult a representative or organizing union before layoffs.

Notification-day sequence: 8-K or press release (if any), then the leader's internal announcement, then one-to-one notifications starting in the earliest time zone, then survivor meetings, then customer outreach by account teams, with the holding statements on standby.
After notification day: update the FAQ daily for the first week, staff the help desk, log WARN and authority notices with proof of delivery, and hold survivor one-to-ones and team check-ins.

notes: Every message comes from one approved business rationale and the documented selection record. Inconsistent reasons across managers, FAQs and public statements are the main evidence of pretext in RIF litigation.

The Disclosure Committee gate comes first. A RIF can be MNPI: restrict the planning group, put everyone involved under blackout, and time internal and external messages with any 8-K (Item 2.05) and Regulation FD obligations.

In consultation countries, announcing individual selections before the process is complete can void dismissals (Germany §17 KSchG), defeat meaningful consultation (China, Vietnam, Taiwan) or trigger union disputes (Israel). The global announcement must say those countries are still in process.
Sequence across time zones so nobody learns from the press, an access cut or a colleague. Notify in one-to-one meetings on the same day for each decisional unit, never by mass video call.

Visa holders need same-day Immigration support. Since the September 18, 2026 executive order made layoffs a factor in H-1B and LCA adjudication, Immigration also reviews the RIF's effect on pending petitions.

US employees keep NLRA Section 7 rights to discuss the layoff and their terms of employment. Social media reminders may cover only MNPI and genuinely confidential information, not talking about the RIF itself.
Localize everything: letters, FAQs and announcements in the local language, local dates and currencies, and local support such as job-seeking leave and unemployment documents.
Survivors decide whether the RIF damages retention. Hold team meetings the same day and one-to-ones within the week, and promise 'no further cuts' only when it's true and approved.

countryNotes.us: Federal WARN applies at 100+ employees: 60 days' notice to employees, the state dislocated-worker unit and local officials. Group releases need OWBPA decisional-unit disclosures (45 + 7 days), and H-1B exits need LCA withdrawal, USCIS notice and a return-fare offer.
countryNotes.us-ca: Cal-WARN covers establishments with 75+ employees and layoffs of 50+ within 30 days regardless of percentage: 60 days' notice to employees, EDD, the Local Workforce Development Board and city and county officials, with SB 617 content. Final pay, including vacation, is due on the separation date, together with the UI Code 1089 notice and DE 2320.
countryNotes.us-co: No mini-WARN; federal WARN notices go to employees, CDLE and the local chief elected official. Final pay with all accrued vacation is due immediately, and confidentiality terms in group releases must meet the POWR Act.
countryNotes.us-nc: No mini-WARN; federal WARN notices go to employees, the NC Commerce dislocated worker unit and the chief local elected official. Final pay is due by the next regular payday, and pay cuts used instead of layoffs need written notice one pay period ahead.
countryNotes.us-tx: No mini-WARN; federal WARN notices go to employees, TWC and the local chief elected official. Layoffs count as discharges, so final pay is due within 6 calendar days (Labor Code 61.014).
countryNotes.us-wa: The WA mini-WARN (chapter 49.45 RCW) applies at 50+ full-time WA employees: 60 days' notice to ESD and to employees or their union. Employees on PFML can't be selected except under the statutory exceptions, and volunteers who respond to a written RIF announcement can claim UI (HB 2264).
countryNotes.ca: An Ontario mass termination (50+ in 4 weeks) needs Form 1 before notice is effective, 8, 12 or 16 weeks' notice and a workplace posting; employees get 3 unpaid job-seeking days. A BC group termination needs notice to the Minister, and individual ESA and common-law notice applies in both provinces.
countryNotes.de: Works council consultation must be complete before a full §17 KSchG notice goes to the Agentur für Arbeit, and defects void every dismissal. Add the Interessenausgleich and Sozialplan, a §102 hearing per employee and wet-ink notices, and tell no one they are selected before the gates open.
countryNotes.il: No WARN regime, but each employee needs an individual hearing (shimua) with a written invitation, and protected employees (pregnancy, reservists) need permits. Consult a representative or organizing union before layoffs, and never time a RIF to undermine organizing.
countryNotes.in: Retrenching 'workers' requires 1 month's notice with reasons, notice to the government, retrenchment compensation, the Re-skilling Fund payment and a 1-year re-employment preference. Offices below the Chapter X thresholds need no prior permission, and full-and-final settlement is due within 2 working days.
countryNotes.tw: File the ESA Art. 33 notice 10 days before each layoff; mass redundancy thresholds require a plan 60 days ahead and negotiation. Give Art. 16 notice with paid job-seeking leave of up to 2 days a week, and the involuntary separation certificate, all in Chinese.
countryNotes.cn: Art. 41 layoffs need a 30-day explanation to the union or all employees and a report to the labor bureau, with priority-retention groups and 6-month rehiring priority; the union must be notified before any unilateral termination. Most MNCs use mutual termination at N-plus packages instead.
countryNotes.vn: Structural or economic terminations need an Art. 44 labour-use plan consulted with the union and published within 15 days, and 30 days' notice to the provincial People's Committee and the employees. Pay the job-loss allowance (1 month per non-UI year, 2-month minimum) and settle within 30 days, with all documents in Vietnamese.
